notes: §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR4 makes REWRITE ... FROM "equivalent to the execution of the following statements in the order specified": "MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1" under the MOVE statement's rules, then "The same REWRITE statement without the FROM phrase." SequentialIoBinder.BindRewrite binds the phrase through MoveBinder.BindFromPhrase, which hands identifier-1 and record-name-1 (the record named, not the widest record of the area) to BindMoveOf, the one application of the MOVE rules; SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRewrite emits that bound move first and then the code path a REWRITE without FROM takes. No edition arm in the move; the one 1985 difference is the gate VersionConformancePass.VisitRecordFromPhrase, which refuses FROM literal-1 and FROM a figurative constant at --std 85 (COBOL0871), since the 1985 format prints only identifier-1. The witness rewrites from a shorter and a longer alphanumeric item, a numeric item to a numeric record, a JUSTIFIED RIGHT record and a group. Probed further at --std 85 on a sequential file: the move is done even when the REWRITE then fails (no READ before it, status 43, and the record area holds the moved value); a numeric sender aligns on the decimal point (12.34 to 9(4)V9(4) stores 00123400), a COMP sender converts, a subscripted and a reference-modified sender and an alphanumeric function follow MOVE; an alphanumeric-edited or alphabetic sender to a numeric record draws COBOL0819 and an index data item COBOL0809. A sender in the record's own storage draws nothing; that is the syntax rule §1985:VII.4.5.3 SR1, kb/Work PB5077, not this rule.

next.reason: 2023 adds FROM literal-1 (§2023:14.9.35.4 GR7: "MOVE literal-1 TO record-name-1"), which the 1985 format refuses; the FROM identifier-1 case is unchanged. 1985 REWRITE GR4: REWRITE FROM = 'MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1 according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement', then REWRITE without FROM. §2023:14.9.35.4 GR7 states the same two steps ('MOVE identifier-1 TO record-name-1 ... according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement'); §2023:14.9.35.3 SR6 restates the MOVE-validity part. literal-1 and the FILE form are additions outside 1985 programs.
